key_insight: Mach 4 flow over a microscale cylinder exhibits independent bow-shock pulsations and a Reynolds-dependent wake transition from no clear unsteadiness to vortex shedding and then higher-frequency oscillations.
engineering_relevance: These instability regimes can inform assessment of unsteady aerodynamic behavior around microscale bodies in supersonic rarefied flows.
method: Direct Simulation Monte Carlo for a 30 μm cylinder at Mach 4 and Reynolds numbers 270–6750.
Power spectral density analysis at discrete flow probes.
Dynamic mode decomposition of flowfield snapshots.
evidence_signal: Probe spectra and flowfield decomposition identify 10–15 MHz bow-shock pulsations across all cases, while wake modes shift from St ≈ 0.2 toward dominant St ≈ 0.5 oscillations as Reynolds number increases.
watch_item: The proposed link between bow-shock pulsation frequency and shock standoff distance remains tentative, and the reported regimes are specific to the studied conditions.
paper_title: DSMC Study on Unsteadiness of Supersonic Flow Over a Cylinder
